### 1 — Scene
A breakfast: fried eggs, grilled tomato and mushrooms, toast, banana, yogurt, strawberries, milk, and a milky hot drink. I exclude the cereal on the separate plate at the right, following your instruction about food on other plates.

### 2 — Vessels
- Main plate: approximately **22 cm diameter**, area **380 cm²**.
- Strawberry bowl: approximately **11 cm diameter**, area **95 cm²**.
- Toast and banana sit directly on the tray; I estimate their footprints separately.
- Bottle, mug, and yogurt pot are estimated from their visible dimensions and fill levels.

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Percentages below refer to each item's own plate or bowl. For food directly on the tray, footprint area is used instead.

| Item | Area coverage / footprint | Gross volume calculation | Density (g/ml) | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Two fried eggs | 40% of plate = 152 cm² | 152 × 0.7 = 106 ml | 0.95 | 101 | 190 | 192 |
| Grilled tomato halves | 22% = 84 cm² | 84 × 1.5 = 126 ml | 0.65 | 82 | 25 | 21 |
| Cooked mushrooms | 8% = 30 cm² | 30 × 1.0 = 30 ml | 0.65 | 20 | 35 | 7 |
| Toast, one slice | About 100 cm² | 100 × 1.0 = 100 ml | 0.30 | 30 | 265 | 80 |
| Banana, edible portion | About 90 cm² | 90 × 1.8 = 162 ml | 0.70 | 113 | 89 | 101 |
| Sliced strawberries | 60% of bowl = 57 cm² | 57 × 1.6 = 91 ml | 0.60 | 55 | 32 | 18 |
| Yogurt in small pot | Approximately 25 cm² cross-section | 25 × 4 = 100 ml | 1.0 | 100 | 80 | 80 |
| Milk in bottle | Approximately 18 cm² cross-section | 18 × 5 = 90 ml | 1.03 | 93 | 50 | 47 |
| Milky coffee or tea | Approximately 40 cm² cross-section | 40 × 5 = 200 ml | 1.0 | 200 | 20 | 40 |

The main plate's coverage totals **70%**, consistent with the visible uncovered rim and gaps. No separate butter or oil portion is clearly visible; modest cooking fat is included in the cooked-food energy estimates.

### 8 — Sanity check
Estimated total: **794 g and 586 kcal**, including drinks; approximately **501 g of food excluding the milk and hot drink**. This is plausible for the visible breakfast. Yogurt type and the amount of milk in the hot drink are the largest energy uncertainties.
